findings.message: This round moved the 'unsuccessful deployment' rule into contracts.ts as `unsuccessfulDeployment`, and its doc comment says it is "One rule for Delivery and every module reading ReleaseDeployed". The line under the new re-export still has a second, hand-written copy of that rule: `unsuccessfulSql = sql.raw("('rolled-back', 'failed')")`. portfolio.ts:43 uses that copy to pick where a release is now. The two copies can drift apart. Fix: build the SQL list from one shared constant (for example, export `UNSUCCESSFUL = ["rolled-back", "failed"] as const` from contracts.ts, then derive both `unsuccessfulDeployment` and `unsuccessfulSql` from it).
findings.scenario: A later change adds a new unsuccessful status (say 'aborted') to `unsuccessfulDeployment` only. The board, the Overview and Leave treat an 'aborted' UAT deployment as unsuccessful, but the portfolio query (portfolio.ts:43) still reports the release as sitting in UAT.

findings.message: The fix for stageNote writes its wording as a new inline ternary: `back.status === "failed" ? "Failed in" : "Rolled back from"`. It does not use the shared `StageWord`/`stageWord` from deployment-status.ts, which the pill, the chip and the board track use, and which the previous finding asked for. That makes a second copy of the status-to-word mapping. Any other unsuccessful status will read "Rolled back from". Fix: build the note from `StageWord(back.status)`.

fix_proof.reason: no review.test_command configured, so no test could prove the fix
